title: Interleaved sparse KV eviction causing device-side slab fragmentation under continuous batching
creator: Diego Soto
description:
Summary:
We are seeing gradual GPU RSS growth and sustained resident slab fragmentation in workloads that interleave very sparse KV cache reads (few KB per request) with periodic large-generation batches. Symptoms appear after ~6–8 hours under continuous batching and do not reproduce with purely large or purely small request streams.

Why this ticket: several previous allocator investigations focused on bulk-prefetch or dedupe hot-slices, but this pattern looks like an interaction between the KV eviction flow, per-request tiny allocations, and cudaMallocAsync's async-free lifecycle causing small slabs to be orphaned across streams. This ticket captures a reproducible case, telemetry, hypotheses, and a plan for targeted mitigations.

Observed behavior (telemetry):
- GPU RSS increases by ~10–15% over long runs; top-resident arenas are small-size slab buckets (8KB-64KB).
- cudaMemPool metrics (via CUPTI + cudaMemGetAttribute) show a rising count of "deferred frees" and growing outstanding allocation count in the async pool despite overall application allocation rate flattening.
- Per-stream allocation timelines show short-lived allocations created on high-priority inference streams but freed asynchronously on background worker streams; free callbacks delayed by scheduling; staged allocator retains blocks in a pinned "staging" sub-pool.
- KV cache eviction pattern: many tiny evictions (evict 2–8 entries) triggered during large generation windows; these evicted entries cause immediate small re-allocations on subsequent requests.
- Host pinned staging usage increases when sparse eviction rate is high; we see higher host->device pinned allocations concurrently with slab fragmentation.

Steps to reproduce (dev cluster):
1) Start continuous batching runner with mixed workload: 80% long-gen requests (seq_len 1024–2048), 20% sparse KV read requests (seq_len 32, KV touch size 4–12KB).
2) Enable per-process cudaMemPool and allocator tracing: heap timeline, pool-resident counts, stream->alloc-id mapping, and RTV event traces.
3) Run for >6 hours; capture nvtx annotated traces and periodic cudaMemPool stats. Repro rate ~70% on p4d and A100 nodes with current runtime-1.21.

Initial findings / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Mixed-size eviction churn prevents slab coalescing because small allocations become orphaned across multiple size classes; the slab coalescer is conservative to avoid races and therefore never compacts.
- Hypothesis B: async free path depends on stream completion callbacks which are delayed due to priority inversion: inference streams preempt background worker streams which process the free callbacks, leading to transient residency accumulation that becomes long-lived when combined with slab bin fragmentation.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache eviction and immediate prefetch/repopulation keeps working set bouncing across size classes, preventing reuse and causing the allocator's small-pool greedy retention to hold onto lots of small slabs rather than returning them to the device pool.

Experiments run so far (results):
- Experiment 1: Force synchronous frees after KV eviction (synchronize stream after evict) -> lower RSS in short run but adds ~3–8ms p99 latency to sparse requests, unacceptable for SLOs.
- Experiment 2: Increase coalescer aggressiveness (merge across adjacent bins at compile-time) -> reduced number of orphan slabs but introduced a race on concurrent alloc/free; required locks caused a throughput regression.
- Experiment 3: Introduce epoch reclamation (periodic global sweep on low-load) -> temporarily reduced fragmentation but did not eliminate leak under steady mixed churn.

Proposed next steps (priority order):
1) Implement a lightweight deferred-free pump in the runtime: free callbacks will enqueue to a low-latency reclamation worker pinned to a high-priority stream capable of processing async frees without major scheduling inversion. Target: process frees within 100ms under normal load.
2) Add a small-pool fragmentation metric exposed in Console: percent of pool blocks below 2x average utilization per-size-class and count of single-slab non-coalesced blocks. This will allow alerting for gradual drift.
3) Modify KV eviction to batch tiny evictions into grouped reclaim operations (aggregate and free N entries in single operation) to reduce number of tiny allocations/frees crossing streams.
4) Add a runtime config knob: "aggressive_small_slab_return" that will force the allocator to return idle small slabs back to the CUDA pool earlier when residency exceeds threshold; guarded by telemetry and default off.
5) Create e2e test harness that runs mixed workload for 24h in CI infra (nightly job) and fails if GPU RSS growth > 5% or fragmentation metric crosses threshold.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproducer no longer shows steady-state RSS drift after 12 hours in 95% of runs on both A100 and H100 nodes with continuous mixed workload.
- Console fragmentation metric reported and dashboard created; regression alerting wired to SLO channel.
- Patch implementing deferred-free pump and grouped KV eviction in runtime landed behind feature flags and validated on a canary pool with no >5% throughput regressions on high-volume tests.

Risks / trade-offs:
- Processing frees on a higher-priority reclamation worker risks adding jitter to inference streams if reclamation work saturates the stream — mitigate by rate limiting and accounting.
- Returning small slabs to CUDA pool more aggressively may increase allocation churn and slightly raise p50 latency for cold requests; we will gate with feature flag and telemetry.
